question: Why is a semiconductor diode considered a non-ohmic device? Give reason.

options.A: A diode is non-ohmic because its current is directly proportional to the applied potential difference, although it conducts differently in forward and reverse bias.
options.B: A diode is non-ohmic because it has zero resistance in both forward and reverse bias.
options.C: A diode is non-ohmic because its current is not directly proportional to applied potential difference and its $V-I$ relation is non-linear.
options.D: A diode is non-ohmic only because it is made of a semiconductor, irrespective of its $V-I$ relation.
